title: CONNECT-IP Forwarding and MTU Policy Architecture
purpose: Define RFC 9484 CONNECT-IP forwarding checks, route matching, Hop Count and TTL handling, link-local forwarding suppression, IPv6 MTU policy, and ICMP forwarding-error decisions.
design_summary: `Http3ConnectIpForwardingPolicy` centralizes received-packet admissibility, additional filtering, route matching, forwarding-error classification, encapsulation-only Hop Count or TTL decrement, link-local forwarding suppression, IPv6 MTU minimums, ICMPv6 echo MTU probing, low-QUIC-MTU stream abort policy, and ICMP forwarding-error signaling helpers.
data_and_state_considerations: The helper is stateless and accepts caller-provided route ranges, policy flags, and MTU observations. Live routing tables and outbound interface selection remain adapter-owned.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Invalid or policy-denied packets are forwarding errors rather than protocol violations.
Self-generated packets and decapsulation do not decrement Hop Count or TTL.
IPv6 tunnel MTU must be at least 1280 bytes and QUIC DATAGRAM IPv6 conveyance aborts below that boundary.
risks: Actual ICMP packet construction remains adapter work.
Operational DSCP, congestion-control, authentication, and registry policies remain separate RFC 9484 slices.
